surfaces.part: eye chart board (white panel with frame, blue top strip, letters, red line)

answer.evidence: The object is a flat wall-mounted chart. Its silhouette is a uniform 14px-wide rectangle across rows 2-27. The frame outline is at rows 2 and 27, with a blue strip at row 4 and a white face with letters below. There is no ellipse, no front-edge line followed by eave shadow, no roof, and no visible contents. The blue strip at row 4 is a decorative stripe on the vertical face. Because it is a wall-mounted flat object, it is drawn as a front elevation with no top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small white chart board with black letter marks and a thin dark outline. All of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral (100%), so the outline is a neutral black/grey line, the 'sticker' look, while the hedge, stall and well references lean toward tinted material outlines (0-33% neutral). It has about 3 lightness steps on the board (white, light grey, dark) and no per-material ramp, with no grain, speckle or wood texture on the frame or post. The measured 8 tones per tile is not far below the hedge (9), but those tones come from the letter glyphs and not from shading. It is well below the stall (17) and well (20), which show 5-6 step ramps and per-element texture. Judged by eye, the piece looks flatter and thinner than the references and would read as a sticker beside them.

surfaces.part: eye chart board (white panel with frame and blue header strip)

answer.evidence: The chart is a flat rectangular board, 14 px wide, drawn face-on from rows 2-27. It has a dark outline, a blue header strip at row 4, white paper with black optotype letters (rows 5-19), a red line at row 21 and grey dashes at row 23. There is no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no visible side face. The board is a flat vertical plane, which is acceptable for a wall-mounted object. It reads as a front elevation, not a three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small white board with black chart glyphs and a thin dark frame. The facts show 8 visible tones per tile, but they are spread over a tiny sprite. By eye the white panel has only 2-3 lightness steps, with no grain, speckle or per-part shading. The outline and frame are neutral black: 100% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 0-1% for the tinted hedge and cheese stall. The Beodeul props (hedge, stall, well) show 5-6 steps per material, clustered texture and tinted dark-material edges. The candidate reads as a flat sticker next to them. It is also much thinner than the stall and well, so sparseness is not the only issue: the board and its stand have no wood grain or shading ramp. The 0% near-flat coverage comes from the glyphs breaking up the panel and does not reflect real texture.

surfaces.part: eye chart board (white panel with blue top stripe, letters and red line)

answer.evidence: The chart is a flat rectangular board, 14px wide and rows 2-27, drawn face-on. Its dark outline and frame are the only edges. The blue stripe at rows 3-4 is a printed header band, not a horizontal top surface: it has no front-edge line or eave shadow, and the width profile is constant at 14 from row 2 to 27. The white face with letters, red line and grey squares is a vertical face. No ellipse, roof or contents are visible, and no side face is drawn. For a wall-mounted flat picture this is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small white chart on a thin pole. It has a neutral dark outline all the way round (100% near-neutral dark edge pixels, no brown or tint). Its body is a white panel with black letter glyphs, and the pole and base are barely shaded. That gives about 3 real lightness steps against 5-6 on the references. The measured 8 visible tones per tile come mostly from the black glyphs and the outline, not from material shading. The panel has no grain, speckle or per-material ramp, and the wood frame is a single tone. The hedge, well and stall references all show tinted outlines, several-step ramps and surface texture. The lamp reference is also neutral-outlined, but it is a thin metal post, so it does not excuse a panel prop that looks like a sticker. Next to the references the candidate looks flatter, thinner and more sticker-like.

The candidate's 8 tones come from a very small area, but by eye it is a flat white board with a few black glyph rows and only 2-3 lightness steps on the board and frame.
